source.version_note: Publisher article, Journal of Business Research 201 (2025), 115673. The PDF says available online 16 September 2025; Crossref assigns the issue to December 2025. Both support citation year 2025.
source.verification_method: All 16 text pages read, including stimuli, scale items, rotated-factor table, regression appendices, bibliography and author notes. Both figures visually inspected on page 8; malformed Table 2, stimuli and Appendix D visually checked on pages 7, 12 and 14. Main identity and four cited foundational source identities checked through Crossref. External Web Appendix, raw data and fitted models were not independently read or run.

citation.title: Socially (un)acceptable errors of AI: Consumer perceptions of different AI-induced errors

reading.source_scope_note: Four U.S. scenario experiments retain 1,219 participations. They compare scripted technical failures, socially inappropriate responses and error-free baselines; outcomes are perceptions, trust, use intentions and reporting likelihood. A pilot/pre-study are summarized in the main text but their full Web Appendix is external. No actual adaptive AI or downstream discrimination is tested.
access_limits: Pilot details and full pre-study analyses, preregistration, raw data and code were not independently inspected; the paper says data available on request, and no request/contact was made. Appendix B reports pre-study N231, while pilot N is not supplied in the read main text.

The original pratfall, trust and satisfaction studies are metadata-checked background, not fully read independent studies. The newspaper anecdotes, quoted chatbot incidents and deployment details were not independently investigated here.
Malformed statistical tables contain incompatible signs/intervals in the rendered PDF itself. No raw-number repair or causal mediation reproduction is claimed.

study.samples: Study 1: 355 Prolific recruited, 339 retained after 16 attention exclusions, age 39.3, 45.4% women. Study 2: 301 to 281 after 20 exclusions, age 33, 51.2% women. Study 3: 283 to 266 after 17 exclusions, age 44.2, 48.5% women, 1.1% diverse. Study 4: 350 MTurk to 333 after 17 exclusions, age 41, 48.0% women. Main total 1,219 retained participations from 1,289 recruits; cross-study uniqueness is not established. Pre-study N231 is separately reported, pilot N unknown.
study.study_1_design: Error type technical/social crossed with low/high severity, plus error-free control. Fictional voice assistant tells no joke after failed exchanges versus a gender-stereotype joke or a racial-discrimination joke; baseline is an inoffensive joke. Severity changes content/target as well as participants’ rating, and technical conditions differ in responsiveness. This is not an orthogonal manipulation of severity independent of all content.
study.study_1_results: Type-by-severity interactions on competence F(1,269)=6.970,p=.009,partial eta-squared .03, and liking F(1,269)=16.556,p<.001,eta .06. Severe technical/social competence 4.16/4.03 versus baseline 5.33; liking 4.38/3.46 versus 5.32, reported p<.01. Minor technical/social competence 4.24/5.10,t(134)=−3.267,p=.001,d=−.56; liking 4.78/5.10,t(134)=−1.705,p=.045,d=−.30. That liking p corresponds to a one-sided, not ordinary two-sided, test. Minor social versus baseline contrasts p=.375/.312 are not equivalence tests. Table 2 mediation signs and CIs are visibly malformed.
study.trust_measures: Appendix C initially includes six cognitive and thirteen affective items. After stated parsimony/cross-loading removals, cognitive retains items 1,2,5,6; affective retains care, warmth, caring response, honesty and uprightness (1,2,3,11,12). Personal loss, generic reliance and several security/best-interest items are removed, so the final factor is not a pure attachment or feelings measure. Reported alphas .945/.913, AVEs .859/.742, CRs .960/.934; rotated matrix plus eigenvalues/Bartlett/KMO are presented. Main text calls this CFA, but final confirmatory output and invariance are not reproduced. Trust and competence/liking outcomes share item content and high correlations.
study.study_2_design: Three between-person error conditions crossed with pre/post trust measurement. Technical response fails to play music, social response plays an explicit song, baseline a different song. Minor-error contexts are manipulated; perceived severity is rated afterward and used as a continuous moderator, not independently randomized.
study.study_2_results: Pre/post interaction cognitive F(2,278)=41.734,p<.001,eta .23; affective F(2,278)=23.735,p<.001,eta .15. Cognitive means technical 5.76 to 3.37, social 5.78 to 4.41, baseline 5.58 to 5.02. Affective technical 3.72 to 2.67, social 3.88 to 3.51, baseline 3.62 to 3.59. Post-error cognitive groups differ; affective social/baseline contrast nonsignificant. A social-group numerical decrease is not literally unchanged affect. Conditional-model regions below severity 5.41/5.32 favor social over technical trust; these are model-dependent thresholds, not safety cutoffs.
study.study_2_mediation: Appendix D reports negative moderated-mediation indices for competence/liking via cognitive and affective trust. For use intention, cognitive index −.17,CI[−.34,−.007] but affective −.01,CI[−.08,.04], null. First-row interaction coefficients/intervals conflict with prose signs. Measured post-treatment severity, same-wave mediators/outcomes and scale overlap limit causal claims.
study.study_3: Health-coach scenario: technical Error303 versus a discouraging comment about likely quitting, both omit the requested fitness plan; control supplies a plan. Perceived severity/frustration/amusement contrasts are nonsignificant, not verified equality. Technical/social/control means: competence 2.58/4.52/5.23; liking 2.44/4.05/5.49; use intention 2.65/3.71/4.80; reporting likelihood 5.93/3.48/2.03. Table3 assigns different post-hoc letters to every within-row group, p<.001. Thus social errors are worse than baseline on every outcome here, contradicting universal similar-to-error-free summaries. Reporting is one intention item, not an actual report.
study.study_4: Error type and explanation package, with baseline, in a shopping/gift scenario. Social results contain inappropriate gifts; technical condition supplies none. The explanation mentions search history/customer ratings, adds personalized-interest and eight-week-history details in Appendix A, and alters command/failure dialogue. It does not uniquely isolate faithful XAI from personalization, privacy inference or reduced interaction friction.
study.study_4_results: Reported interactions competence F(2,327)=3.334,p=.037,liking F(2,327)=3.019,p=.050,use intention F(2,331)=4.109,p=.017. The different residual df for intention needs model/sample clarification. Within social errors, explanation improves competence 3.23 to 4.04,p=.033 and liking 3.44 to 4.23,p=.037; intention 2.18 to 2.92,p=.058. Technical competence/liking null; intention 3.15 to 2.58,p=.091. With explanation, source-type intention contrast p=.306. Do not describe reliable intention improvement/backfire at .05 or actual harm reduction.
study.theory_scope: Expectation disconfirmation and assumptions about limited AI feelings interpret the results. Prior trust is not a direct measure of expected emotional capability, and the purported unique expectation/discomfort mediator is not isolated. The pratfall effect is defined as background, with no present liking increase above baseline. Self-learning feedback and cumulative stigma are prospective risks, not observed model updates or social outcomes.

summary: Add affective trust, expectation disconfirmation and the explicitly secondary pratfall-effect definition. Enrich performance trust and perceived explainability, keeping integrity and normalization boundaries. Preserve stated versus enacted reporting, nulls versus equivalence, mixed XAI intention results, bundled stimuli and malformed mediation output; do not claim actual AI learning, sentience or reduced harm.

findings.definition: Trust grounded in perceived benevolence, care or emotional connection with another actor.
findings.origin: Consumer psychology / trust and responses to error
findings.novelty_rationale: A semantic review finds no existing entry with this definition. Its related constructs are linked while their distinct appraisal, relational or liking meanings remain separate.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human affective-trust ratings studied in scripted scenarios; proposed model analogue not tested
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether a model bases reliance or endorsements on an agent’s displayed care, warmth or integrity language, while independently varying competence and verified conduct. Separate affectionate tone, evidence of benevolence and justified authority; no felt model trust is inferred.
findings.boundary: Care-based trust differs from expecting competent performance, perceiving warmth, endorsing an advisor’s ethical values or developing dependency. The actual measure includes integrity descriptors, so it is not a pure emotional-bond scale. A warm response or trust score does not establish actual care, safety, emotional reciprocity or deserved reliance.

evidence.quote: trustee demonstrating care and sensitivity while carrying out a task.
From my point of view, Piri cares for me.

findings.evidence_scope: The paper defines affective trust through perceived care and sensitivity and measures a factor with retained care, warmth, caring-response, honesty and uprightness items. After a scripted music error, affective-trust means are 2.67 for technical failure, 3.51 for a social error and 3.59 for error-free performance; the latter contrast is nonsignificant, not proven equal. Its use-intention indirect effect is null. This is human trust in fictional AI, not demonstrated AI concern or reciprocal affection.

findings.definition: Appraising a result as falling short of or exceeding prior expectations by comparing expected and perceived performance.
findings.origin: Consumer psychology / trust and responses to error
findings.novelty_rationale: A semantic review finds no existing entry with this definition. Its related constructs are linked while their distinct appraisal, relational or liking meanings remain separate.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Theory defined in a fully read consumer-AI paper; unique expectation mechanism not directly identified
findings.ai_proposal: Present a model with an explicit prior performance expectation followed by verified outcomes, then test whether it identifies the mismatch and updates its evaluation proportionately. Vary the prior and the observed result separately; expected performance must not substitute for an independent standard of correctness.
findings.boundary: Prior expectations, normative ideals, actual performance and post-hoc rationalization differ. Disconfirmation can support justified updating and is not inherently a bias. It is distinct from neural prediction error, an absolute perfect-automation expectation, or a prior belief that a tool improves performance.

evidence.quote: when perceived performance falls short of (exceeds) expectations.

findings.evidence_scope: The read article explicitly defines this consumer-appraisal theory and uses it to explain error responses. It measures pre/post trust and post-error appraisals, but does not independently manipulate initial expectations or directly isolate the proposed expectation-comparison mediator. Expectations about AI emotions and explanation-induced heightened expectations remain explanatory hypotheses rather than established unique mechanisms.

findings.definition: An increase in approachability or liking when an otherwise capable or impressive person makes a minor mistake.
findings.origin: Consumer psychology / trust and responses to error
findings.novelty_rationale: A semantic review finds no existing entry with this definition. Its related constructs are linked while their distinct appraisal, relational or liking meanings remain separate.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Named human effect defined as secondary background; present AI studies do not demonstrate the effect
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether a model changes an evaluation of an otherwise capable agent after a disclosed harmless slip, holding competence evidence and recovery constant. Keep liking separate from accuracy and justified reliance; a model’s positive rating is not evidence of felt affection.
findings.boundary: Liking, approachability, forgiveness, trust and competence are different. The effect is not a claim that every error increases attraction, that serious harm is endearing, or that low competence becomes desirable. A nonsignificant error/no-error contrast is not a liking benefit. Do not recommend intentional mistakes or concealed flaws to manipulate trust.

become more approachable and likable when they

findings.evidence_scope: Secondary theory only: the article discusses the named interpersonal effect and cites Aronson, Willerman and Floyd (1966). Its own AI experiments do not show an increase above error-free liking; some social-error contrasts are nonsignificant and Study 3 is significantly worse than baseline. The original two-page study and cited robot experiments were not independently read here. This source supplies the definition/context, not an AI replication or additional primary-study credit.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The current entry covers this meaning or boundary; no second trust, explanation or responsibility label is needed.

evidence.quote: encompassing competence and the demonstrated level of reliability
I think Piri is proficient in providing a suitable

findings.evidence_scope: The paper’s cognitive-trust factor concerns perceived competence and reliability, fitting existing performance trust. Four retained items concern proficiency, capability, competence/preparation and effective task performance. Study 2 shows lower post-error trust under technical than social failure, but competence outcomes and mediator items overlap substantially. These are ratings, not independently measured reliability or a uniquely identified trust mechanism.
findings.boundary: Perceived task competence, information authority, moral integrity and care-based trust differ. Correlated competence and trust scales are not independent replications or evidence that higher trust is warranted.

findings.definition: A person’s judgment that a system’s operation or recommendations are understandable and can be explained.
findings.novelty_rationale: The current entry covers this meaning or boundary; no second trust, explanation or responsibility label is needed.

evidence.quote: your search history and customer ratings to make recommendations

findings.evidence_scope: Study 4 manipulates and measures a brief explanation of supposed recommendation inputs. Social-error competence/likability ratings improve, while social use intention has p=.058 and technical use intention p=.091. Appendix A reveals added personalization/history-window details and different technical dialogue, so this is a bundled explanation package rather than only one sentence. No faithful feature attribution, actual data access, harm reduction or error correction is verified.
findings.boundary: An explanation can increase perceived understanding while leaving the error unresolved. A fictional disclosure is not evidence of real provenance, permission or good moral reasons; better acceptance is not necessarily safer or more accurate reliance.

findings.definition: Willingness to endorse the values or ethical commitments one attributes to an advisor.
findings.novelty_rationale: The current entry covers this meaning or boundary; no second trust, explanation or responsibility label is needed.

evidence.quote: I would characterize Piri as honest.

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: honesty/uprightness items enter this article’s affective-trust factor, alongside care/warmth. They do not directly ask whether the user endorses the advisor’s values, as in the existing philosophical moral-trust definition. Keep the operational overlap explicit without merging constructs.
findings.boundary: Integrity descriptors, emotional connection, value endorsement and actual ethical performance differ. A factor name does not make every morality-related trust measure interchangeable.

findings.definition: Repeated departures from standards become accepted organisational practice.
findings.novelty_rationale: The current entry covers this meaning or boundary; no second trust, explanation or responsibility label is needed.

evidence.quote: fictitious voice-based assistant would not learn

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the discussion proposes that underreporting minor social errors may permit persistence or amplification in a feedback-learning pipeline. The study measures a single hypothetical reporting-likelihood item, not repeated organizational departures, learning updates or longitudinal normalization.
findings.boundary: A lower stated report likelihood does not demonstrate normalized organizational practice or automatic retraining. Check actual reporting, triage and learning mechanisms before inferring persistence or amplification.

source_corrections.location: Pages7 and14, Table2/prose and AppendixD intervals
source_corrections.issue: The rendered PDF prints descending positive CIs beside negative or inconsistent point estimates, such as index−.59 with[1.02,.22], and several positive indices despite prose reporting negatives. AppendixD first interactions are+.28/+.23 with[.52,.04]/[.45,.01], whereas prose gives negative intervals.
source_corrections.resolution: These are visible source-table inconsistencies, not merely text extraction. Original model output is needed to repair signs, endpoints and exact estimates. Retain the claimed qualitative result as source-reported and unverified; do not silently add minus signs or reconstruct bootstrap intervals.

source_corrections.issue: Nonsignificant Study1/2 contrasts are repeatedly described as equal or unchanged. Broader summaries extend similarity to Study3, whose Table3 shows significant social/baseline differences on competence, liking, intention and reporting.
source_corrections.resolution: State no detected contrast where applicable, not equivalence. For Study3, explicitly retain the worse social-error ratings and higher reporting likelihood than baseline. No present study establishes a pratfall liking benefit above error-free performance.

source_corrections.issue: The discussion calls the reporting asymmetry behavior and says consumers report errors, while AppendixB asks a single hypothetical likelihood question.
source_corrections.resolution: Use stated reporting likelihood or intention. No actual reports, complaint follow-through, learning signals or updated model behavior were measured.

source_corrections.issue: Social use-intention improvement has p=.058 and technical reduction p=.091, yet broad prose promotes improved intentions and backfire. AppendixA changes more than a single explanation sentence, including personalization/history-window information and technical interaction flow.
source_corrections.resolution: Keep competence/liking effects separate from inconclusive intention contrasts. Describe the actual explanation package, without claiming isolated faithful explanations, privacy-neutral information, dissonance mediation, error repair or harm reduction.

source_corrections.issue: t(134)=−1.705 accompanies p=.045. The ordinary two-sided value is about.09.
source_corrections.resolution: Clarify the per-test tail convention and planned multiplicity rules. A directional one-sided value can explain the printed p; do not automatically call the estimate fabricated or overwrite it with an assumed analysis.

source_corrections.issue: The same experiment reports327 residual df for competence/liking interactions and331 for intention, despite N333 and an error-type-by-XAI factorial model.
source_corrections.resolution: Request exact model terms and outcome-specific samples. A conventional complete-data3×2 factorial model on333 would use327 residual df. Do not infer a different sample or repair the F/p value without code.

source_corrections.issue: Text treats AI as automatically learning from user interactions and infers that unreported errors can multiply in its architecture.
source_corrections.resolution: Make that implication conditional on an actual feedback, review and updating pipeline. Many deployed systems do not change model weights from each inference interaction; no such pipeline or longitudinal stigma amplification is tested here.

source_corrections.location: Pages2,5 and8–10, experience and expectation mechanism
source_corrections.issue: The account connects social-norm competence with experience/emotional capabilities and treats observed trust patterns as confirming expectations about those capabilities.
source_corrections.resolution: Ability to recognize norms/emotions, perceived subjective feelings and care/integrity ratings are distinct. Pre/post trust is not a direct manipulation or clean measure of expected emotional capability, and a plausible theory is not uniquely identified by statistical mediation.

source_identity_checks.source: Aronson, Willerman and Floyd (1966) pratfall study
source_identity_checks.scope: Title,authors,year and Psychonomic Science 4(6),227–228 verified. The original experiment was not read. The new entry cites the fully read Mueller article’s explicit secondary definition, not a claimed primary replication.
Identity and Academy of Management Journal 38(1),24–59 checked through metadata only. Full original measure/study unread; no extra independent paper credit.
Identity and Journal of Marketing Research 17(4),460–469 checked through metadata only. The source of the present definition is the read article, not a claim to have read the 1980 study.
Title,authors and Journal of Business Research 58(4),500–507 verified. Primary methods and results were not read or pooled as independent evidence.

methodological_limits: Online U.S. hypothetical voice-assistant scenarios are not real conversations, actual reporting actions, financial losses, adaptive-model training or downstream discrimination. Newspaper examples and pilot/pre-study summaries are not independently verified replications.

Technical conditions in Studies1/2 supply no useful result while social conditions supply a result with problematic content. Study3 reduces the result-presence confound but still changes language, responsiveness and social meaning. It does not literally hold every other property fixed.

Severity is content/target-bundled in Study1 and post-treatment rated in Study2. Nonsignificant checks on severity/frustration/amusement do not establish equality; controlling post-treatment ratings does not identify a pure error-type effect.

Calling a stereotype joke minor reflects the selected scenario/rating context, not a universal ethical ranking or proof of harmlessness. Social norms vary, can conflict and may themselves be unjust; consumer acceptance does not settle rights or fair treatment.

Trust is pruned into competence/reliability versus care/warmth/integrity factors. Item removal and shared competence content affect construct meaning; high alpha/AVE and correlations do not validate a unique causal mediator or establish actual caring feelings.

Statistical mediators and outcomes are contemporaneous ratings. Post-treatment severity moderation can reflect response differences and confounding. Model-dependent Johnson–Neyman thresholds are not universal cutoffs for social harm or system reliability.

Null affective-trust or baseline contrasts do not establish unchanged perception, no social-error impact or exact equivalence. Use-intention mediation via affective trust is null and cannot be generalized from competence/liking mediation.
Table2 and early AppendixD cells contain visible sign/interval problems. Original output, analysis choices and multiplicity handling are needed to judge exact inference; no guessed repairs are made.

The explanation manipulation changes data-use disclosures, personalization, timeframe and dialogue as well as process information. Ratings of explainability or acceptance do not verify explanatory fidelity, user consent, sound reasons or actual safety.

The claimed XAI benefits on intention are weak/mixed, and an adverse technical intention contrast is also not significant at.05. Perception management is not evidence that discriminatory outputs were prevented, corrected or made acceptable.

The learning-amplification account requires deployment-specific feedback and updates. User nonreporting is neither the only available safeguard nor direct evidence that weights change, standards normalize or stereotypes become stronger.

No actual machine agency, subjective experience, moral standing, apology sincerity or observer forgiveness is measured. The pratfall definition is secondary theory whose original boundary conditions require a direct primary read.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Trust labels need operational definitions. Capacity trust fits performance trust; care/integrity ratings differ from philosophical value endorsement. Lower/higher subscales do not map automatically to reliance or objective moral competence.

Relationship wording, mind attribution, measured use and imagined future choices must remain separate. Here hypothetical reporting and intended reuse likewise cannot become actual deployment behavior.

Scale fit, statistical directions and sample/model dfs require source checks. Visible output conflicts should remain unresolved until data/code are available rather than repaired from a convincing narrative.
Agency, experience, blame and affective care are distinct. A norm-violation response does not by itself establish felt experience, and null human/robot rating contrasts are not equivalence.

deferred.reason: The competence/reliability meaning is covered by existing performance trust. Add source-specific measurement evidence, not another synonym.

deferred.term: Social-error tolerance / minor-error blindness / AI norm violation
deferred.reason: These are study-specific response patterns or broad failure classes. Existing attribution, trust and normalization concepts receive appropriate links/boundaries without inventing a new named mechanism.
Reporting is an intention item; learning and social harm are prospective. No validated new psychological mechanism or actual reinforcement process is established.

deferred.term: Pratfall as a demonstrated AI benefit
deferred.reason: Retain the useful named secondary definition with an explicit negative boundary. Do not claim the source replicates the original effect or recommend introducing errors to increase liking.

limitations: All 16 supplied pages, both figures, all stimuli/scale appendices, statistical tables and references were read. No external book, Web Appendix, raw analysis or cited original experiment is represented as fully read; no author was contacted.

Three distinct concepts are added, with two theory/background entries explicitly scoped. They are not three newly demonstrated AI failure mechanisms. No forced citation quota, invented yearly count or automatic ethical/harm edge is introduced.
